Europe Faces Social Unrest Fueled by Affordability and War

Social unrest has spread across Europe, originating in France and extending to countries like Albania. The protests, initially sparked by student anger over an understaffed and overcrowded education system, have broadened to encompass concerns about affordability, perceived government inaction, and a widening wealth divide. The unrest is occurring against a backdrop of war and debt, with some reports suggesting that Europe's far right is gaining traction amidst this instability, particularly in relation to anger over rising fuel prices ahead of elections.
